tasks.q: List the title of every game in the table.
brief: The table games holds one row per game, with the columns title, kind, players and minutes; the starter code fills it from the lines typed in.
Write one query giving one column, title, for every game, in the order the rows are stored.
Print each row the query finds on its own line, values separated by single spaces.
tasks.starter:
import sqlite3
db = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
db.execute('CREATE TABLE games (title TEXT, kind TEXT, players INTEGER, minutes INTEGER)')

# These lines fill the table from the input. Leave them as they are.
rows = []
line = input()
while line != 'END':
    title, kind, players, minutes = line.split(',')
    rows.append((title, kind, int(players), int(minutes)))
    line = input()
db.executemany('INSERT INTO games VALUES (?,?,?,?)', rows)

# Your query, and the printing of the rows it finds, go below.

tests.why: SELECT names the column you want and FROM names the table. Every game appears because there is no WHERE to narrow it down.
The same query must work whatever is in the table - if this fails you have typed the titles out instead of querying them.
A shorter table, same query. SELECT title gives one value per row, so print that value on its own.

tasks.fb: SELECT says which columns and FROM says which table - with no WHERE, every row comes back.

teach.say: SELECT names the columns and FROM names the table. db.execute() hands back one row at a time, and a row is a group of values.
code: for row in db.execute("SELECT name FROM pet"):

forbid: in rows
The answer has to come from an SQL query. Looping over the rows list in Python does the work the query is meant to do.

info.title: Asking, not telling
info.text: SQL says what you want, not how to get it. The database works the steps out for itself.

info.title: Quotes matter
info.text: WHERE kind = card looks for a field called card and fails. WHERE kind = 'card' looks for the word.

info.title: Boundaries again
info.text: 'Over 60' and '60 or more' are different queries. The off-by-one that bites in Python bites here too.

info.title: Use brackets
info.text: WHERE a AND b OR c can mean two different things, and brackets say which one you meant.

info.title: Sorting text
info.text: ORDER BY on a text field sorts alphabetically, which is how a list of names is put into order.

info.title: Why a database
info.text: A database holds far more than a program's memory, and many people can query the same table at the same time.
